show_hn.title: Show HN: I wrote an email app that accepts only one sender per inbox
show_hn.story_text:
Infinite inboxes, including prefixes where you don't have to create inboxes before you use them -- they self create when you add a suffix. Three types of inboxes:
- One sender. Locks to the first domain to send email (except gmail, outlook, etc where it locks to an email account for obivous reasons. It bounces everyone else.
- Temporary. Lasts for a while (24h, 7days, etc) then bounces. Received messages stay or go as per your choice.
- Prefix. The most powerful. Declare a prefix like "service" and then invent any suffix, like "service-netflix" or "service$bank" and it creates a new one-sender inbox locked to whoever wrote first. Bring you own domain. Bring your own AI (MCP server ready). Forwarding. Please help me test it.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Parsimony – an open-source benchmark for how much code AI models add
show_hn.story_text: Existing benchmarks measure solve rate and token output/cost, but don't punish excess code, which makes a codebase harder to work with in the long term. I wanted to measure this since it matters most for long-term projects. Method: it takes the patches that benchmarks already publish (DeepSWE, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Live) and counts "coding units": syntax elements like statements, calls, names and literals. I didn't use lines of code, so cramming code isn't rewarded. Deleted code is subtracted, so it measures net units. GPT-6 and Claude 5.5 have no public patches yet, so I ran them myself on 3–10 tasks on my own subscriptions (shown as faded circles, not ranked). show_hn.title: Show HN: Run AI-generated logic safely inside your app
show_hn.story_text: Stof is an open-source runtime for logic you don't own or fully trust. Imagine a JSON document with functions inside, scoped to just the document that contains them. Stof instantiates this doc as a small wasm env, and makes these functions safe to call. They can't access or manipulate anything but their own doc. WebAssembly by itself is large in binary form, requires a lot of tooling, etc. Stof can be sent over the wire easily, is a superset of JSON for compatibility, and keeps the guarantees. I created Stof not to replace a data format or anything, but to be a glue layer for data and distributed systems to work with one another. Show HN: Lowlight – Dim your MacBook keyboard backlight below the macOS minimum
show_hn.story_text: I work in a dark room a lot, and even the lowest keyboard backlight setting on my MacBook was too bright. I noticed macOS fades the backlight all the way to zero when it turns off, but the lowest level it lets you pick is noticeably brighter than that. Lowlight is a small menu bar app that adds extra steps under the macOS minimum, plus the normal range above it. You choose how many extra steps you want. It fades the backlight down and holds it at the step you pick. If you change the keyboard brightness in Control Center, macOS takes back over. It uses private CoreBrightness APIs, so a future macOS update could break it. It's Apple Silicon only, needs macOS 26, is signed and notarized, and is MIT licensed. You can build it from source with ./build.sh. I'm happy to answer ques
